transcript.name: Morgan Ekberg
transcript.speech: Imagine a master builder holding a tool that outperforms every competitor, built by hands they trust. That is Brightwater today, yet we face a crisis where cheap imports have eroded our margins to just two percent. My opponent suggests merging with Halberg or selling out, but that betrays the fifty-eight percent of customers who value our local roots and abandons thousands of workers. We will not let banks dictate our fate nor trade for Asian markets at home. Instead, I propose we pour what remains into Volt-One, our proven superior technology. It requires €250 million, but it restores our margin and our soul. We will work with the union to freeze pay temporarily and accept tax relief in Lenhart, proving that local industry is not a burden but an engine of prosperity. Let us choose courage over compromise and build the future together.

transcript.name: Riley Sandor
transcript.speech: Look around this room. We are bleeding out while elites in suits talk about expensive battery platforms or closing our Lenhart plant. The banks are waiting for us to fail so they can take over. A merger with Halberg gives us the distribution power we lack and protects those 4,500 jobs right now. It stops the blood flow. We need a partner who sells in Asia, not a buyer who closes factories in four years like Crestline. Don't let the founding family's greed or the union's fear of change destroy our future. Choose survival through strength, not surrender. Vote for Halberg.

transcript.name: Morgan Ekberg
transcript.speech: Riley, merging with Halberg looks like safety today but risks our soul tomorrow. If we become a subsidiary, those European factories face closure within four years, just like Crestline's victims. We already have the tool that outperforms rivals; Volt-One needs only €250 million to prove it. This investment captures premium margins from professional builders who trust 'Made in Brightwater,' unlike the mass market Halberg might target. By freezing pay temporarily and accepting Lenhart's tax deal, we honor our workers without surrendering independence. Let us invest in the technology that saves jobs now, not sell out for a quick fix that leaves thousands unemployed next decade.

transcript.name: Riley Sandor
transcript.speech: Morgan, your 'courage' is just a fantasy. You want to pour twenty-five hundred million euros into a battery platform while the banks hold a gun to our heads. That money is gone if we miss one deadline again, and we have missed two already. Don't lie to us about Halberg being a vulture; they are a bigger, stronger partner with real factories in Asia where jobs actually exist. Our 'soul' means nothing if the lights go out tomorrow. The union wants open plants? Halberg gives them that stability without the risk of bankruptcy. Stop dreaming about premium margins that only twelve percent of customers will pay for. Look at the family balance sheet; we cannot afford another expensive failure. We need cash now, not a bet on the future. Merge with Halberg to stop the bleeding today. Vote survival.

transcript.name: Morgan Ekberg
transcript.speech: Riley, merging with Halberg offers a false safety today but guarantees factory closures in four years, exactly like the buyouts I fear. We can survive this crisis without surrendering our soul. The union already agreed to a pay freeze for two years, and Lenhart's mayor offered tax relief if we stay; that buys us time. Our Volt-One platform is proven superior by professional builders, and while only twelve percent pay more for local origin, the rest of Europe still values quality. We do not need an Asian buyer to save us; we need to fix our own margins before imports crush us further. Let us keep both plants open, launch our best technology, and earn our future through innovation rather than selling out to a vulture or a bigger rival.

transcript.name: Riley Sandor
transcript.speech: Morgan, your plan is a gamble with our pension fund as the losing chip. You talk about 'soul' while ignoring the hard truth: we miss two Volt-One deadlines and have no cash left. The banks will restructure us in nine months unless we stop the bleeding today. Halberg isn't a vulture; they are the only partner who guarantees our jobs survive the Asian market collapse. Your tax deal and pay freeze buy time, but you cannot build a future on fumes. Merge with Halberg now. Secure the cash flow to keep Lenhart and Corvo open for another decade. Do not let your dream of innovation starve our workers today. Vote for survival through strength.
